back: GDP: value of goods and services produced inside a country in a year. GNI: GDP plus income from abroad minus income sent abroad. Per capita = divided by population.
A composite index from 0 to 1 combining life expectancy, years of schooling and GNI per capita; very high ≥ 0.800, high 0.700–0.799, medium 0.550–0.699, low < 0.550.

Dimension index = (value − minimum) ÷ (maximum − minimum); education index is the mean of expected and mean years of schooling indices; income uses logarithms; HDI = cube root of (health × education × income).
National averages hide inequality; informal and unpaid work and the environment are omitted; definitions and data quality vary; use several indicators together.
Primary: raw materials. Secondary: manufacturing and construction. Tertiary: services. Quaternary: knowledge and information (research, IT).
As an economy develops, employment shifts from the primary sector to the secondary and then to the tertiary and quaternary sectors.
Choose indicators; collect primary data (questionnaires, observation, mapping) and secondary data (ZimStat, council records); present; evaluate reliability and ethics.
Share of GDP of a sector ÷ share of employment of that sector; below 1 means below the national average.
